newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai mills to produce more whites as prices firm.
newsitem.headline: Thai mills to produce more whites as prices firm.

text.p: Thai mills are seen producing more white sugar this crushing season to cash in on bullish prices as whites premiums rise, industry sources said on Wednesday.
The March/May white premium for 100 ICUMSA was quoted around $18 over London number 5 this week versus about $8 earlier this month, they told Reuters.
Several sugar mill operators told Reuters that they would rather remelt to produce more white sugar if they could under current circumstances.

Heavy Indonesian buying of white sugar was cited for the rise in premiums. Over 200,000 tonnes of sugar had been or would be delivered to Indonesia between January and early February, trade sources said.
An Indonesian government agency said the country would import around 500,000 tonnes of sugar in 1997.

"The white-to-raw premiums of around $68-69 per tonnes is not normally considered that attractive. But with such poor raw premiums (for Thai sugar) and good outlook for white demand, it makes sense to turn to white," said one mill manager in central area.
Thai raw premiums for March/May edged down to 0.30-0.35 U.S. cents over New York on FOB basis from 0.30-0.40 last week.
However, some mills expressed reservations and said they were not going to join the bandwagon so soon.
"The white premiums surge could be short-term due to artificial shortages...The price was pulled up by Indonesia offtake which was mostly for prompt shipment," he said.
"This temporary shortage was also caused by limited white sugar capacity of some mills and jammed ports," he added.
Others who looked at China said the white-to-raw premiums were not attractive enough and they still expected raws prices to improve soon on demand from China.
They said China was likely to import far more than 690,000 tonnes of sugar it announced it would for this year, 350,000 tonnes of which will be from Cuba.
"I would guess the import will be more than a million. It's just the matter of when," said another miller.
On the production side, Thailand's 46 registered mills produced 1.8 million tonnes of sugar as of January 22, 1.14 million tonnes of which were raw and 669,560 tonnes white.

At ports, almost 10 vessels were loading sugar for shipment mostly to Asian destinations while almost 40 others declared that they would arrive for loading between the end of this month and early February. --Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642 reuter ak/ram
